title: Preventing Trap Seal Loss and Sewer Odors
description: A P-trap relies on a standing water seal to block dangerous sewer gases from entering living spaces. Trap seal loss commonly occurs due to siphonage, evaporation in rarely used fixtures, or momentum discharge. To prevent self-siphonage, ensure the drain trap is correctly connected to a vent line according to local code and avoid unvented S-trap configurations. For infrequently used drains, periodic flushing or installing a code-approved trap seal primer maintains the liquid barrier. Understanding trap dynamics ensures indoor air quality and reliable fixture drainage across residential plumbing systems.

A P-trap relies on a standing water seal to block dangerous sewer gases from entering living spaces. To prevent self-siphonage, ensure the drain trap is correctly connected to a vent line according to local code and avoid unvented S-trap configurations. For infrequently used drains, periodic flushing or installing a code-approved trap seal primer maintains the liquid barrier. Understanding trap dynamics ensures indoor air quality and reliable fixture drainage across residential plumbing systems.
